task.description: Produce a rework fix design (a new section or a new file src/design/iss0100-rework1-guard-slug-scoping.md — your choice, but reference it clearly) implementing the ISSUE-FIXER rework diagnosis's recommendation in docs/issue-reports/ISS-0100-rework1-diagnosis.yaml §recommendation_for_fix_design. Specifically: (1) PREFERRED fix layer (2a) — add a new migration (next available GBL-* number after GBL-102; re-check `ls migrations/GBL-1*.sql` at implementation time, do not assume a stale number) that further scopes the ISS-503 guard (currently in migrations/GBL-102_iss503_guard_tenant_type_scope.sql) to ALSO exclude tenant slugs matching the project's informal 'tc-*' test-fixture naming convention — i.e. the guard's WHERE clause becomes storage_mode='LEGACY_RLS' AND tenant_type='production' AND slug NOT LIKE 'tc-%' (or a more precise pattern if the diagnosis's evidence shows a more exact convention — re-verify by grepping tests/integration/ for the actual slug literals used across adp04b/tm0x/other test files before finalizing the exact LIKE pattern; do not just copy 'tc-%' blindly if a more precise anchor exists, e.g. requiring the prefix to be at the start of the string and followed by more structure). Same design decision needed as before: new migration file (following the same rationale as GBL-102's own §5.2 — migrations don't re-run once recorded, so scoping changes need a new file). (2) SUPPLEMENTARY — extend tools/lint_test_isolation.py (read it first) to flag any INSERT INTO tenant / service.createTenant() call site in tests/integration/ whose slug argument does not start with an allowlisted test-fixture prefix (at minimum 'tc-', possibly others already in use — grep to confirm), so the guard's slug-based exclusion has a corresponding enforcement mechanism and doesn't silently break if a future test uses a different naming convention. (3) OPTIONAL, LOW PRIORITY — note in the design (does not need to be implemented in this WF-03 run, can be filed as a follow-on issue) the build.zig test-integration-env naming confusion (env_integration_tests secretly runs the full suite, not a scoped ENV-01..05 subset) documented in the diagnosis's evidence — recommend filing this as its own GitHub issue per the No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directive since it's a genuine, separate, incidentally-discovered defect (misleading step name that cost TEST-RUNNER a wasted verification cycle believing it had isolation when it hadn't), rather than fixing it as part of this fix. This is a SMALL rework — likely 1-2 files (new migration + lint script edit), well within the 5-file constraint, no need for a multi-iteration plan this time.

Design's slug-exclusion pattern is justified against actual grepped evidence of the test-fixture naming convention, not assumed
Design specifies the exact tools/lint_test_isolation.py extension needed
Design recommends filing the build.zig test-integration-env naming issue as a separate GitHub issue (not fixed here)
No implementation code — prose design only
Design explicitly re-confirms this fix does not regress the already-shipped 13-file/GBL-102 fix from the first pass
task.description_rework_2: REWORK 2 (from CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, handoff wf03-iss0100-step-02d, FAIL verdict): CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR independently grepped ALL `INSERT INTO (public\.)?tenant\(` sites in tests/integration/ (not just .createTenant() API calls) and found a BLOCKER: tests/integration/iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig's TC-ISS-107-04 ('check_constraint_rejects_invalid_mode', around line 182-231) inserts a tenant row (slug 'iss107-t4', line 193) via raw SQL that omits both tenant_type (defaults 'production') and storage_mode (defaults 'LEGACY_RLS'). ORCH independently re-read this test and confirmed: the INSERT happens BEFORE the test's `BEGIN`/`SAVEPOINT`/`ROLLBACK` block (lines 201-230), which only wraps the subsequent invalid-storage_mode UPDATE attempt — so the tenant row itself is auto-committed and NEVER cleaned up (no DELETE, no defer, unlike its sibling TC-ISS-107-05 at line ~237 which explicitly deletes its own 'iss107-t5' row). This is a genuine, permanent, guaranteed leak every time this test runs — worse than the transient in-flight leaks from adp04b/tm01 that motivated this whole rework, because it never self-heals. Since 'iss107-t4' is not tc-prefixed, GBL-103's proposed slug exclusion does not cover it, and it would still trip the guard on every subsequent TestHarness.init() in the same binary run. FIX DIRECTION (recommended, but use your judgment): prefer fixing the actual leak over further broadening the slug-exclusion pattern — add explicit cleanup for the 'iss107-t4' row to TC-ISS-107-04 (e.g. `defer h.conn.exec("DELETE FROM tenant WHERE id = $1::uuid", &.{tenant_id_uuid}) catch {};` registered immediately after the INSERT succeeds, matching TC-ISS-107-05's own pattern), since (a) it's a smaller, more surgical fix than continuing to whack-a-mole new slug prefixes into the guard's WHERE clause, and (b) it fixes the actual test-hygiene bug rather than just working around its symptom. If you determine broadening GBL-103's slug pattern is still necessary as defense-in-depth, you may include both, but the iss107-t4 cleanup fix is the primary required change. Also, per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's MINOR finding: your original completeness check searched only for `.createTenant(` plus a hand-picked file list — redo the completeness verification as a blanket grep for every `INSERT INTO (public\.)?tenant\(` occurrence across tests/integration/ (all ~17 files it found, not just the ones you already suspected) and check each one's column list for an omitted tenant_type, to make sure no other permanent leak exists beyond iss107-t4. The validator also flagged tests/integration/iss502_spt_cutover_test.zig and tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig as needing the same audit (both omit tenant_type on some inserts) — confirm whether either has a real leak or is already safely cleaned up, and note the finding either way.

result.summary: Reworked src/design/iss0100-rework1-guard-slug-scoping.md to address CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's second FAIL (handoff wf03-iss0100-step-02d, issue ISS-0100-REWORK1-VALIDATION-01/-02). Added new sections 3.5-3.7: (1) a redone completeness audit as a blanket grep for every `INSERT INTO (public\.)?tenant\(` occurrence across tests/integration/ (17 files, matching the validator's independent count), classifying each by whether tenant_type is explicit or omitted, and for every omitted-tenant_type site confirming cleanup status; (2) an independent re-derivation of TC-ISS-107-04's actual transaction semantics (tests/integration/iss107_tenant_storage_mode_test.zig lines 182-231, cross-checked against vendor/pg/pg.zig's begin/exec/readUntilReady implementation), which found that the row is in fact already rolled back on every code path today (PostgreSQL BEGIN does not nest; the test's own inner ROLLBACK at line 230 undoes the whole outer transaction including the INSERT; h.deinit()'s rollback catches the early-return failure path) -- so the validator's BLOCKER was based on an incomplete transaction-semantics read rather than a confirmed live leak, which the design states explicitly; (3) despite that finding, added the requested defensive fix anyway per the rework-2 handoff's explicit direction and as protection against the fragile/non-obvious mechanism: a `defer h.conn.exec("DELETE FROM tenant WHERE id = $1::uuid", &.{tenant_id_uuid}) catch {};` registered immediately after TC-ISS-107-04's existing INSERT, matching TC-ISS-107-05's own DELETE statement form; (4) confirmed test_iss503_rls_removal.zig and iss502_spt_cutover_test.zig (both flagged by the validator for the same audit) are already safely cleaned up via correctly-ordered defer patterns -- no leak in either. No additional leaks beyond the (already-non-leaking) iss107-t4 site were found anywhere in the 17-file sweep. Final file count for this rework: 3 (GBL-103 migration, lint script T060 check, iss107 test cleanup) -- within the 5-file cap, no iteration split needed.
